subject: Follow-up: deployment options and deployment boundary questions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Julian Park <julian.park@brightscale.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment options and deployment boundary questions

Hi Julian —

Thanks again for the chat earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap from our call
- BrightScale goal: embed a generation endpoint for customer-facing flows (product search assistant). Estimated peak throughput ~500 rps, sustained ~150 rps, p99 latency target ~250ms for single-turn generate calls.
- Primary concern: isolation and predictable latency during spikes ("noisy neighbor" behavior on shared infra is a blocker).
- Secondary: SOC2 evidence, key management, and whether we can do a temporary capacity bump around product launch.

Redwood options (high level)
1) Hosted API (shared pool) — fast to get started, automatic batching and KV caching, good cost profile. Provides published performance profiles for our model catalog but does not include dedicated isolation guarantees. We have smart routing and throttling to reduce interference but cannot contractually promise isolation in hosted.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools with isolation at the serving layer, committed throughput, and SLA options (latency & uptime). Best fit if you need contractual p99/SLA and want predictable tail latency under load.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full isolation, customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations, and the tightest control. Appropriate for regulated workloads or very strict isolation/SLO requirements.

Immediate ask from us
- Can you confirm whether a contractual SLA for p99 latency is a hard requirement for launch, or if an operational SLO (measured / monitored, but not contractual) would be acceptable for the first 3 months?
- Please share your infra/security owner for a technical deep-dive (I believe Sara Lin is the infra contact).

Attachments: I attached our RFI answers (Redwood_RFI_responses_May2026.pdf) that cover SOC2, network diagrams, and example SLA language.

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Dev (our infra architect) + Sara to review traffic profile, KV cache strategy, and test plan.
- If SLA/isolation is non-negotiable: we can scope Dedicated or Private options and put together a brief Mutual Action Plan + ballpark pricing.

Proposed times: Mon 5/4 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue 5/5 14:00–15:00 PT — let me know what works and I’ll calendar.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.com

From: Julian Park <julian.park@brightscale.com>

Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightscale.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment options and deployment boundary questions

Thanks for the summary, Rishi — helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we book the deep dive: 

- When you say hosted has "smart routing" and "throttling," can you point to the specific guarantees? Do you publish p95/p99 numbers for hosted endpoints we can reference in our SLOs?
- If we start on hosted and observe noisy-neighbor incidents during a pilot, can Redwood move us to Dedicated quickly (say within a week)? How does burst capacity work?
- Ballpark: what is the delta in monthly cost we should expect between hosted at our projected usage vs Dedicated for committed capacity? We just need a rough order-of-magnitude to set expectations with finance.

We'd like Sara (infra lead) on the deep-dive. Also can you confirm whether SOC2 reports and your network diagrams are included in the RFI attachment?

-Julian
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightScale Inc.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Julian Park <julian.park@brightscale.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment options and deployment boundary questions

Julian — great questions. Short answers below, and then some concrete next steps.

1) Hosted performance visibility
- We publish benchmarked latency distributions for each model in the catalog (p50/p95/p99) under standard test loads — I included a pointer to the performance section in the RFI. Those are empirical numbers rather than contractual SLAs. Hosted is engineered for low tail latency via continuous batching, KV prefix caching, and model routing.

2) Migration path and burst capacity
- We offer fast migration paths from Hosted -> Dedicated. Typical lead time for a dedicated pool depends on region and GPU availability; with committed intent we can prioritize and often stand up a dedicated pool within 3–10 business days. For launch spikes we offer burst capacity options on Dedicated to cover short-lived peaks. We can detail runbook ops for temporary increases.

3) Cost delta (very rough)
- For your stated profile (peak ~500 rps, sustained ~150 rps): Hosted (metered) tends to be lower up-front; Dedicated is higher fixed commit but gives predictable per-token cost at scale and avoids noisy-neighbor risk. Ballpark: expect Dedicated to be roughly 2–4x the hosted blended cost at the volumes you described if you reserve enough GPUs to cover peak consistently. We'll surface a tailored cost model after the traffic deep-dive.

Next steps I propose
- Book the technical deep-dive: Dev (infra architect) + Sara to review KV cache warmup, request fanout, and test harness. Dev — are you available Mon 5/4 10:00 PT?
- If BrightScale needs a contractual p99 SLA for launch, we’ll scope Dedicated and prepare a short Mutual Action Plan + draft MPA (attached: draft-mpa-redwood.docx).

Attachments: draft-mpa-redwood.docx (mutual action plan template + MSA pointers). RFI includes SOC2 report excerpt and network diagrams.

Appreciate the clarity — happy to map out a short timeline once we confirm the infra/launch constraints.

Best,
Rishi
